findings.message: Totals are marked as a lower bound (`≥`) only when whole transcripts are skipped (`t.skipped > 0`). A record that carries usage but fails to parse is counted in `unreadable` and left out of today, week, session and role totals, yet those totals still print as exact. `lowerBound`, used by `money` and the token counts, ignores `t.unreadable`, so 'could not count' reads as a complete total. This also covers the band and status line, which use `money`. Fix: return `≥` when `t.skipped > 0 || t.unreadable > 0`. Add a table-driven test with a bad usage record, a bad title record and a skipped file, asserting `≥` in the pane, band and status line.
findings.scenario: A transcript holds one valid assistant record ($0.02) and one assistant record with `input_tokens: -1`. scanText counts it as unreadable. The pane shows `today (UTC) 2k tokens · $0.02` and the band shows `$0.02 today, API-equivalent estimate`, with no `≥`, even though the record's spend is missing from the total.

findings.message: `resolveHead(...).catch(() => null)` turns a HEAD read that threw into `null`, the same value used for 'no git repo'. `final()` then draws neither 'at HEAD' nor 'behind HEAD', so a failed lookup looks the same as having no checkout. Consider a distinct 'HEAD unknown' marker for the thrown case.

The AC-7 read-only check only catches the literal pattern `$.fs.<method>` and `$.process`. A write through an alias such as `const { fs } = $; fs.write(...)`, `$['fs'].write`, or an engine parameter not named `$` passes as 'PASS: only read methods'. Either narrow the PASS wording to what the check actually proves, or also grep for `fs.write`, `.write(` and `process` in any form.
